title: Spark rate limits are two-parameter throttles, pairing a maxAmount ceiling with a slope refill rate
content:
Every rate-limited conduit direction in the Spark Artifact is specified by exactly two parameters. A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3.4.1.1.2.4 states that "the current `maxAmount` and `slope` for this conduit's inflow/outflow are defined in the subdocuments herein," and the subdocuments then give an inflow and an outflow pair.

The pairing is what matters. `maxAmount` alone would be a static cap — once consumed, an operator would be permanently blocked or would need a governance action to reset. `slope` supplies replenishment over time, making the control a leaky-bucket throttle: bounded burst capacity that regenerates at a governed rate.

The consequence is that Spark's risk surface is expressed in terms of **velocity**, not merely exposure. A limit can permit large cumulative flows over weeks while making a single large drain impossible — which is the relevant defence against an operator key compromise or a mispriced integration, where the damage is a function of how fast value can leave before humans intervene.

Because both parameters are Atlas-registered per direction and per conduit, changing either is a governance-visible act rather than an operational one.
description: Every conduit direction is governed by maxAmount (instantaneous capacity) plus slope (replenishment per unit time), so limits constrain velocity of capital movement, not just total size.
